Enhancement Shaman Rotation in The War Within

Even with the Midnight changes, Enhancement Shaman can be a little overwhelming at first glance. Since it has more active buttons than the average spec, it means there's a bit of a learning curve when trying to understand how it all comes together. To start, we'll go over some core rules, which will help get you up to speed quickly with your rotational goals. These are listed in order of importance:

Avoid Maelstrom waste: Maelstrom Weapon makes specific spells instant, and is spent at 9+ stacks.Spender used - Lightning Bolt in single target, Chain Lightning in AoE - 

Keep strikes on cooldown: prioritizes Lava Lash, while uses Stormstrike.Filler Priority - Crash Lightning ➜ Stormstrike / Lava Lash ➜ Voltaic Blaze - 

React to procs: Both Hero Talents need to react to the Apex, Storm Unleashed, and some unique procs per build. has Hot Hand, while has both Tempest and Supercharge.

If you're looking for a more bite-sized rotation explanation, check out our simplified guide below:

 Enhancement Shaman Major Cooldowns

While Midnight has brought with it a trim to Enhancement's cooldown suite, there's still a few options available in its arsenal. Making use of them properly is a little more involved than normal, since they don't function as flat increases and influence the rotation. The below sections cover how each cooldown works, and how to get the most out of each use.

 Doom Winds

Doom Winds is your standard cooldown choice, with a 1 minute cooldown and 8 second duration baseline (increasing to 10 with Thorim's Invocation taken) - while also being off the GCD. While active, your chance to trigger Windfury Weapon is doubled, based on your character sheet (so includes the baseline 15%, plus your Mastery chance, and any talent choices that increase it such as Forceful Winds). Additionally, all Windfury Weapon damage you deal while it's active is increased by 20%. This does not impact the bonus attacks from Skyfury.

Important things to know are:
While Doom Winds is active, Main-Hand special attacks rise in value, as they can trigger a Windfury Weapon bonus attack.

Main Hand Strikes are: Stormstrike / Windstrike, Crash Lightning, Sundering / Splitstream and all 3 Primordial Storm strikes.

Each enemy hit by the initial cast of Crash Lightning, and any target hit by Sundering (or Splitstream) count as Main-Hand strikes on each individual target, providing "AoE Windfury Weapon procs". Since Doom Winds increases this chance significantly, it grants truly uncapped AoE when active.
When playing with Primordial Storm, this should always be synced with Doom Winds casts - it provides 3 individual AoE Windfury Weapon triggers,

New in Midnight, this also gains the effects of both Static Accumulation and Thorim's Invocation while active, if taken. The former generates 1/2 stacks of Maelstrom Weapon every second, while the latter gives a way to spend resources through both Stormstrike and Crash Lightning. We go into further detail on how this works in its respective tab.

 Doom Winds

 always plays with Doom Winds as its cooldown, as it naturally lines up with Surging Totem. This window is perfect to overlap with your Hot Hand triggers, as it allows you to generate a huge surplus of Maelstrom Weapon through Static Accumulation, and spend it efficiently through Thorim's Invocation. This, in turn, extends the buff for a significant duration with Totemic Momentum, and is a key part of the new Midnight rotation. While active, it has a few simple rules:

Always weave Lava Lash on cooldown during this, making sure Hot Hand has been triggered from Whirling Fire.
Cast Activators in between. Priority is Crash Lightning ➜ Stormstrike, which should provide cooldown reduction through Elemental Tempo.

 Ascendance

Ascendance and Deeply Rooted Elements are a choice node capstone, which replace Doom Winds if selected. When triggered, this transforms you into an air ascendant, converting your Stormstrike into Windstrike and auto-attacks into Windlash. Both of these attacks have a 30-yard range, are considered special attacks, and ignore your target's armor. Additionally, Windstrike gains the benefit of any talent that benefits Stormstrike, and its cooldown is reduced by 60% while active. Depending on which talent is taken, there's a few different things to know:

Both these also gain the effects of both Static Accumulation and Thorim's Invocation while active, if taken. The former generates 1/2 stacks of Maelstrom Weapon every second, while the latter gives a way to spend resources through both Windstrike and Crash Lightning. We go into further detail on how this works in its respective tab. These talents are always taken in conjunction with this node, and turns the window into a race to cast Windstrike as much as possible when active.

 Stormbringer Ascendance

Due to the heavy Maelstrom Weapon generation while active, Stormbringer can often find it struggles to drain it off with Thorim's Invocation triggers alone. Especially with Thunder Capacitor and Supercharge refunds considered, it will often lead to situations where you overcap, but there's no way of draining it faster. In Midnight, Thorim's Invocation always spends up to 10 stacks with Raging Maelstrom taken, so just cast it on cooldown. In both Single-target and AoE, it follows these rules::

Cast Crash Lightning as a priority, and Windstrike otherwise. Even if Tempest procs, trigger it with Thorim's Invocation as normal.

 Thorim's Invocation

In Midnight, we have multiple ways of triggering Thorim's Invocation - both through Ascendance like before, and through Doom Winds. This is an exceptionally powerful effect, allowing us to siphon our Maelstrom Weapon through other GCDs that generate it, condensing two casts into one. When paired with Static Accumulation granting generation every second during these windows, it leads to explosive cooldown power, high burst, and an overflow of resources. The basic function is:

The Maelstrom Weapon spender cast is dictated by a few specific conditions, and setting which ability is used is known as "Thorim's Invocation Priming". This works as follows under these conditions:

In Midnight, it's good to know what you're currently primed to, but with the removal of addons it's quite difficult to know for sure. You already want to be in the correct state before you cast these, as fixing it while they're active forces you to use up a valuable GCD on the appropriate spell. In most cases, you should naturally be in the correct state through your rotation, and especially in the case of your opening Tempest via Descending Skies will adjust it to the current situation anyway.

 Sundering

In Midnight, Sundering takes the place on the tree as your mid cooldown burst tool, and inherits the same follow-up talents and bonuses that Primordial Wave did previously. It comes with a 30-second cooldown (and no longer incapacitates), and deals a large amount of direct Flamestrike damage to targets in a line in front of you. These hits can trigger weapon imbues, including Windfury Weapon. This is a staple talent in all builds due to Whirling Elements, but also flexes as a high damage burst AoE button.

Surging Elements causes Sundering casts to grant 15% Haste for 12 seconds whenever cast, and also generates 5 Maelstrom Weapon instantly. This is often layered over other cooldowns, and the extra resources it grants makes it an excellent setup tool as well. Note - this does not trigger from Splitstream as .

Casting Sundering with Primordial Storm taken grants a 15-second buff window, replacing the keybind with a powerful 4-step AoE attack. When cast, this consumes (and scales) with all current Maelstrom Stacks, and deals a series of attacks in a fixed order Fire ➜ Frost ➜ Nature ➜ Lightning Bolt / Chain Lightning. Each of the first three elemental strikes are considered AoE Main-Hand hits (so can trigger Windfury Weapon separately), and it then selects Lightning Bolt or Chain Lightning based on the number of targets hit by the initial strikes. Note - this is not activated by Splitstream as .

Depending on the Hero Talent tree taken, the ability serves a variety of functions, but we always aim to use it on cooldown every 30 seconds:

 Stormbringer - makes use of this as a strong front-loaded burst cooldown in AoE situations, using the Haste provided by Surging Elements to empower Ascendance. Unfortunately, it struggles to fit it into single target builds.
 Totemic - always takes this due to interactions with Whirling Elements. The additional Haste it can layer over both Surging Totem and Doom Winds consistently makes an already strong combo of cooldowns even more powerful.

 Surging Totem

Exclusive to , Surging Totem has been re-situated as a burst cooldown tool in Midnight. It retains its 25-second duration, but the cooldown has been bumped up to a minute while having the damage adjusted appropriately too. Now that it's broke free from the shackles of being a maintenance buff, it adds an explosive second layer to your burst windows when playing it. When cast, you'll gain 4 buffs - 3 of which come from Whirling Elements:

Executing these sequences to set up for a long Hot Hand through Totemic Momentum is key, and gives a lot of breathing room after it ends. This often leads to a buff so long it lasts until your next Sundering when played correctly, so aim for that. Sequencing changes between single target and AoE, but follows something similar to this:

Executing this sequence in Midnight consistently is relatively easy, as cooldowns should be kept in sync with correct play. Making sure you don't drift Sundering away from these 1-minute timers is important though, as having the extra Searing Totem active for your upcoming streak of Lava Lash casts contributes a lot of extra damage currently.

Comment by Gormogon
This guide is a great starting point, but needs some final touches. For example, in the legendaries page I can read in Doom Winds' discription: 

The burst window in AoE of banking up Maelstrom Weapon to make use of the Chain Lightning cooldown reduction and cast Crash Lightning 3 times a window with a final Sundering (all of which procs Windfury on all targets hit by the initial casts) makes for a massive opener that we otherwise don't have access to.

But nowhere in the rotation page does it mention that said legendary alters your aoe priority while it is active, making Crash Lightning your highest priority because it will proc windfury on all targets hit. If I went by what the aoe priority mentions, I would drop windfury totem, and then maintain a priority of casting as many hailstormed frost shocks as I can, even during Doom Winds' effect. During aoe doom winds, each crash performs 15-30 hits at once(depending on number of targets) so practically resets us to 10 mw stacks every cast. So a proper Doom Winds window is actually:

 Wf totem -> Crash (gives 10 mw stacks) -> chain -> chain -> crash(back to 10 mw) -> chain -> sundering -> final crash (squeezed in just barely, less so as haste levels increase).
 If anywhere during this you get super unlucky and a crash doesnt get you to 10 mw, just move sundering accordingly to replace the chain that you wont have stacks for. the sundering also procs wf on all targets, so you are guaranteed to be able to follow up. This is also why you don't sunder immediately to get it on cooldown faster, because its your backup to not lose dps if rng messes with you.

The guide makes no mention of this, so a Doom Winds window following the guide's aoe priority looks like this:

Wf totem -> sundering -> crash (to apply buff) -> chain -> frost shock -> chain -> crash -> chain

As you can see these are 2 very different windows, with the 2nd producing significantly less DPS
